title: Credit for a delegated outcome is a counterfactual contrast, not a label read off the trace: randomise the two messages that cross the orchestrator-executor boundary (the brief and the return) at matched tool budgets and executor instruction, and split the delegation loss between them with the two-player Shapley value
abstract: In causal inference the credit of a treatment for an outcome is the contrast between the outcome with the treatment and the outcome without it for the same unit; only one of the two is ever observed, so the individual contrast is unidentified and the average contrast is identified only when assignment is randomised (exchangeability), and when several contributors share an outcome their credits are the Shapley values, the average marginal contribution of each over every order of inclusion, the unique split that is efficient, symmetric and gives a dummy nothing (Hernan and Robins ch. 1-2 as taught in the WIN course notes; Airiau, cooperative games lecture 7). Carried into L4, that says the two messages that cross a delegation boundary, the orchestrator's brief going down and the executor's return coming up, are the units whose credit for a lost item is in question, and that credit is identified only by replacing each message with its counterfactual at random (the harness passes the user's item verbatim instead of the orchestrator's rewritten brief; the harness appends the executor's opened URLs, HTTP failures and stated confidence to the bare answer) while the tool budget and the executor's tool-use instruction are held equal to the single agent's. The lane's two new cards hold the gap: 2611.16526 reports a 9-11 point post-cutoff delegation loss in a grid whose arms differ in total search budget (up to twice) and in the executor's instruction, then attributes the loss to four LLM-judged failure rates without any swap ('may contribute', sec. 5.3); 2611.13254 states that its control-reach table 'is not a measured intervention' and the attribution corpora it audits label a 'responsible agent' from trace reading, with 45% of one split ending in a harness crash the labels assign to an agent. Pre-registered: with budget and instruction matched, the post-cutoff delegation loss is at most half of the paper's (judgment 0.5), and of what remains the brief channel carries a Shapley share of at least 0.6 (judgment 0.5); the result that changes a belief is a matched loss under 2 points (the headline is a protocol artifact), a return-channel share of at least 0.6 (the fix is the return schema, and brief distortion is a symptom), or an interaction term as large as either main effect (no single message is responsible, and a single 'responsible agent' label is unidentified by construction on this testbed).

sentences: Credit is a contrast between two outcomes of the same unit: 'An individual causal effect exists when $Y^{a=1} \neq Y^{a=0}$ for an individual', where $Y^{a}$ is the outcome the unit would have had under treatment level $a$; an average causal effect is present when $\mathbb{E}[Y^{a=1}] \neq \mathbb{E}[Y^{a=0}]$; and because 'we can only observe one of the two counterfactual outcomes for each individual', 'individual causal effects cannot generally be identified', which 'is why causal inference is fundamentally a missing data problem' (WIN course notes on Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If, ch. 1, secs. 1.1-1.2).

The average contrast is identified by randomising who gets the treatment: 'We say the treated and untreated are exchangeable when' $Y^{a} \perp\!\!\!\perp A$ for all $a$, where $A$ is the treatment actually assigned; 'This random assignment ensures that treatment is independent of all variables', measured and unmeasured; 'When exchangeability holds, association equals causation' and 'In a randomized experiment, the observed association is an unbiased estimate of the causal effect'; when randomisation is conditional on a covariate $L$, 'Conditional randomization guarantees conditional exchangeability but not marginal exchangeability', and standardisation or inverse-probability weights $W^{A} = 1/\Pr[A \mid L]$ 'create a pseudo-population in which treatment is marginally randomized' (same notes, ch. 2, secs. 2.1-2.4).

When several contributors share one outcome, the credit of each is its Shapley value: for a value function $v$ on coalitions of the player set $N$ with $|N| = n$, 'the value of agent $i$ in coalition $C$ is the average marginal value over all possible orders' in which agents join, $\mathrm{Sh}(N, v) = \sum_{\pi \in \Pi(N)} \mathrm{mc}(\pi) / n!$ with $\Pi(N)$ the set of permutations and $\mathrm{mc}_i(\pi) = v(\{\pi(j) : j < i\} \cup \{i\}) - v(\{\pi(j) : j < i\})$ the marginal contribution of $i$ to the agents before it; it is efficient ($\sum_{i \in N} \phi_i = v(N)$), symmetric ('When two agents generate the same marginal contributions, they should be rewarded equally'), gives a dummy only its stand-alone value, is additive ($\phi(N, v + w) = \phi(N, v) + \phi(N, w)$), and 'The Shapley value is the unique value that satisfies axioms DUM, SYM and ADD' (Airiau, Cooperative Games lecture notes, ch. 6, pp. 63-65).
sources: https://ucdavis.github.io/win/chapters/01-introduction.html — WIN course notes, 'Chapter 1: A Definition of Causal Effect', built on Hernan and Robins, Causal Inference: What If (fetched 2026-11-15; individual and average causal effect; the missing-data statement)

https://ucdavis.github.io/win/chapters/02-randomized-experiments.html — WIN course notes, 'Chapter 2: Randomized Experiments' (fetched 2026-11-15; exchangeability, randomisation, association equals causation, conditional randomisation, standardisation and IP weighting)

https://www.lamsade.dauphine.fr/~airiau/Teaching/CoopGames/2012/shapley.pdf — S. Airiau, Cooperative Games, lecture notes ch. 6 'The Shapley value' (fetched 2026-11-15; definition as average marginal contribution over orders, axioms DUM/SYM/ADD, efficiency, uniqueness theorem 6.2.2, pp. 63-65)

import_sentence: In causal inference and econometrics, the question of who gets the credit for an outcome is solved by a counterfactual contrast, the outcome with the contributor included minus the outcome with it excluded, identified by randomising inclusion (never by reading the record afterwards) and split among several contributors by the Shapley value, the average marginal contribution over every order of inclusion; carried into L4, that says the orchestrator and the executor are not the units to credit for a lost item, the two messages that cross the boundary are, the brief $B$ going down and the return $R$ coming up, and their credit is the contrast obtained by randomly replacing each with its counterfactual (the user's item passed verbatim in place of the rewritten brief; the executor's opened URLs, HTTP failures and stated confidence appended to the bare answer) in a $2 \times 2$ factorial run at the single agent's tool budget and tool-use instruction, with the two-player Shapley split $\phi_B + \phi_R = L$ of the matched delegation loss $L$ saying how much of the loss each message carries and the interaction saying whether any single message can be called responsible at all.

predicts.statement: Setup: the GDP dataset of 2611.16526 rebuilt from its stated source (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.KD.ZG, the same 30 four-country sets, year 2019 pre-cutoff and 2025 post-cutoff, $N = 60$ prompts, $n = 240$ items, numeric ground truth within 0.1 percentage points) plus the post-cutoff Books set (Goodreads 2026, $N = 20$, $n = 100$), one web interface (SerpAPI search plus open_url) with search results cached on day 1 so every arm sees the same web, one open model (gpt-oss-120b on vLLM, temperature 1.0 as in the paper), $r = 5$ runs per prompt per arm. Arms: $A_0$ single agent, paper protocol ($2n$ searches, $3n$ opens pooled); $D_u$ forced delegation, paper protocol (unmatched: 2 searches and 3 opens per executor, the executor's 'only call a tool if you are not sure' instruction); and the matched factorial $D(b, r)$, $b, r \in \{0, 1\}$, where $b = 1$ means the orchestrator writes the brief and $b = 0$ means the harness passes the user's item text verbatim, $r = 1$ means the executor returns only its final answer and $r = 0$ means the harness appends to that answer a deterministic block (URLs opened, HTTP status of each, the executor's one-line stated confidence), with the pooled budget $2n$ searches and $3n$ opens shared across executors through a global counter and the single agent's instruction given to every executor. Quantities, per item $i$ and arm $a$: $p_i(a) = \Pr[\text{item } i \text{ correct under } a]$ estimated from the $r$ runs. Unmatched loss $\Delta_u = \bar p(A_0) - \bar p(D_u)$; matched loss $L = \bar p(A_0) - \bar p(D(1,1))$; cutoff difference-in-differences $\mathrm{DiD} = [\bar p(D)_{\text{post}} - \bar p(D)_{\text{pre}}] - [\bar p(A_0)_{\text{post}} - \bar p(A_0)_{\text{pre}}]$, which on the paper's own Table 1 reads $(0.66 - 0.77) - (0.75 - 0.77) = -0.09$ for forced delegation. Two-player Shapley split of $L$ with $v(S) = \bar p$ when the lossy channels in $S \subseteq \{B, R\}$ are active: $$\phi_B = \tfrac{1}{2}\big[(v(\emptyset) - v(\{B\})) + (v(\{R\}) - v(\{B, R\}))\big],$$ $\phi_R$ by symmetry, $\phi_B + \phi_R = v(\emptyset) - v(\{B, R\})$, where $v(\emptyset) = \bar p(D(0,0))$, $v(\{B\}) = \bar p(D(1,0))$, $v(\{R\}) = \bar p(D(0,1))$, $v(\{B,R\}) = \bar p(D(1,1))$; interaction $I = v(\{B,R\}) - v(\{B\}) - v(\{R\}) + v(\emptyset)$; the residual $v(A_0) - v(\emptyset)$ is the cost of context separation itself with both messages made lossless. P1 (protocol share): on the post-cutoff sets $L \le \Delta_u / 2$. P2 (channel credit): $\phi_B / (\phi_B + \phi_R) \ge 0.6$ post-cutoff, with $|I| \le \min(|\phi_B|, |\phi_R|)$. P3 (label identifiability): for items where $A_0$ is correct and $D(1,1)$ is wrong in at least 4 of 5 runs (the 'lost items'), the share whose outcome flips under exactly one channel swap is under 0.5, so a single responsible message exists for fewer than half of the lost items. Intervals: 95% percentile bootstrap over prompts, $B = 1000$, as in the paper, plus the run-to-run component reported separately.
predicts.expected: Judgment, not evidence: probability 0.5 that P1 holds (matched loss at most half the unmatched loss), 0.3 that it is between half and the full loss, 0.2 that matching changes nothing. Probability 0.5 for P2 (brief carries at least 0.6), 0.3 that the return carries at least 0.6, 0.2 that the interaction is as large as a main effect. Probability 0.45 for P3. Expected mechanism: post-cutoff, the model's parametric memory is wrong by construction, so (i) the executor instruction 'only call a tool if you are not sure' converts confident wrong memory into skipped searches, a protocol effect removed by matching, and (ii) what survives matching is the brief, because a rewritten brief folds a wrong guess into the executor's task (2611.16526 sec. 5.1, Table 3: correctness of added author attributes 95 to 0 pre to post for GPT-5), and the executor cannot tell a guess from a given; the return channel matters less because the orchestrator in this design has no tool and nothing to do with a reported failure except re-delegate.
predicts.field_assumes: 2611.16526 assumes its two arms isolate the boundary ('we isolate the effect of delegating tool access on performance', sec. 2) and attributes the loss by rates ('may contribute to the observed lower accuracy', sec. 5.3), naming the return side as the fix ('targeted mechanisms for communicating evidence and resolving conflicts', sec. 6) and ruling the full-trace return out by assumption ('would undermine the context-saving benefits', sec. 7); no swap, no matched budget, tokens uncounted. The attribution literature assumes a 'responsible agent' and 'decisive step' exist per failed run and are readable from the trace by humans or judges (2505.00212; 2604.22708; BLADE 2610.18780 'identify the responsible agent and decisive error step'), with 2611.13254 conceding that its reach table 'is not a measured intervention' and 2610.17747 showing judges follow surface cues. The field's own assumption is the reverse: a reading of the record identifies nothing; only an assignment the record did not choose does.
predicts.belief_changing: If $L \le 2$ points post-cutoff, the 9-11 point headline of 2611.16526 is a budget-and-instruction artifact, and every same-model orchestration comparison must match the pooled tool budget and the executor instruction before claiming a boundary effect (a protocol change for 2604.02460's and 2601.11327's successors as well). If the return channel carries at least 0.6, the brief-distortion account (sec. 5.1) is a symptom and the return schema is the recipe, with the fields that pay named by their marginal contribution at matched tokens. If $|I| \ge \min(|\phi_B|, |\phi_R|)$ or P3 holds, no single message is responsible for most lost items on a controlled testbed where every counterfactual was actually run, so a single 'responsible agent' label is unidentified by construction, and attribution benchmarks need an intervention-identified label beside the human one. If the brief carries at least 0.6 and $L \approx \Delta_u$, the paper's reading stands with an identified number and a verbatim-brief recipe: a footnote.

identifiability: Random given: fixed item text, fixed model and weights, fixed sampling (temperature 1.0, top-p 1.0, as in 2611.16526 App. A), fixed cached web (the SerpAPI results and opened pages are frozen on day 1 and served from the cache to every arm, so the web is not a time-varying confounder across arms; without the cache, arm order and run date would be confounded with search results). Assignment: each (prompt, run) is assigned to an arm by the harness at random, so $Y^{a} \perp\!\!\!\perp A$ holds by construction (exchangeability), and the contrast $\bar p(a) - \bar p(a')$ is an average causal effect of the protocol arm on item correctness; within the factorial, $b$ and $r$ are assigned independently, so each main effect and the interaction is identified. Whose temperature: both orchestrator and executor at 1.0; the quantities are mean contrasts, not variances, so they remain defined at temperature 0 (a party at temperature 0 has zero decision variance and a nonzero contrast), unlike the variance splits of CL-W43-14 / CL-W45-08; the run-to-run component is reported beside the contrasts, not inside them. Property of what: $\phi_B$, $\phi_R$ and $I$ are properties of the (model, harness protocol) pair, since the brief and return channels are protocol choices; they are reported per model and per protocol and never as 'the model's'. $L$ versus $\Delta_u$ is a property of the paper's protocol. The residual $v(A_0) - v(\emptyset)$ is the cost of context separation with both messages lossless, a property of the model. Verbatim brief and deterministic return block are harness-written, so the swap changes the channel, not the model's behaviour upstream of it. Judge versus verifier: item correctness is exact numeric (GDP within 0.1 points) or exact title match (Books) against public ground truth; no LLM judge anywhere; the paper's four judged rates are not used. Caveats recorded: the verbatim-brief arm removes the orchestrator's decomposition step too (for GDP and Books the items are listed in the user prompt, so decomposition is trivial and the arm is a brief swap, not a planning swap; on interdependent tasks it would not be); the return block is one choice of fields, so $\phi_R$ is a lower bound on what a return channel can carry, and a second block (full executor trace, the paper's 'extreme') is a sensitivity arm at its token cost.

probe.design: Step 1 (about 25 GPU-hours, 7 days including 4 of harness work): rebuild the GDP (60 prompts, 240 items) and post-cutoff Books (20 prompts, 100 items) sets from their public sources with the paper's year splits; build the single-agent and orchestrator-executor harness with a global budget counter, a verbatim-brief switch, a deterministic return block and a day-1 web cache; run gpt-oss-120b on vLLM (2 H100) across the six arms ($A_0$, $D_u$, four $D(b, r)$ cells) with $r = 5$: 80 prompts x 6 arms x 5 runs = 2,400 prompt-runs, about 40k tokens each, about 24,000 cached-or-live searches (about $350 SerpAPI); compute $\Delta_u$, $L$, DiD, $\phi_B$, $\phi_R$, $I$, the lost-item flip table for P3, prompt-bootstrap intervals and the run-to-run component. Step 2 (about $450 API, 2 days): the same six arms on GPT-5 for GDP only (the paper's largest loss cell, 0.89 to 0.35), to check that the shares are not one open model's. Step 3 (about 5 GPU-hours): the full-trace return arm $D(1, \text{trace})$ with tokens counted, to put the paper's 'extreme' on the same ruler. Optional step 4 (about $200): the pre-cutoff GDP arms on GPT-5 to complete the matched DiD.
probe.dollars: about $350 SerpAPI plus about $90 H100 spot for steps 1 and 3; about $450 GPT-5 API for step 2; about $1,100 in all
probe.days: 11 days: 4 of harness and dataset rebuild, 3 of runs, 2 of analysis, 2 for the GPT-5 arm
probe.kills_if: Dead as an import if, on the post-cutoff sets, both channel swaps move item accuracy by under 2 points with 95% prompt-bootstrap intervals covering zero and $L$ is within 2 points of $\Delta_u$: then neither the messages nor the protocol carry the loss, the loss sits in context separation itself (the residual $v(A_0) - v(\emptyset)$), the messages-as-players framing has nothing to credit, and the result is a footnote saying the fresh executor context, not what crosses it, costs the points. Dead as a ruler (parked, re-open with the full 120-prompt Books set) if the run-to-run component at temperature 1.0 gives per-cell interval half-widths above 5 points at $r = 5$, since then the four factorial cells cannot be told apart at this budget. Dead if the rebuilt GDP single-agent accuracy differs from the paper's gpt-oss-120b cell (0.92 pre) by more than 10 points, since then the testbed is not the paper's and nothing about its headline is being tested.

papers.title: When Does Latent Communication Pay? A Causal Audit of Relayed KV Caches in Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.trick: Replace the key-value cache one agent relays to another with a mismatched-example, zeroed or moment-matched random cache and re-run, so the gain credited to 'latent thoughts' is tested as a contrast rather than read off a benchmark delta; where the receiver needs the sender's private information the contrast is at ceiling, where it does not a pre-registered equivalence test finds no example-specific transfer.
papers.did_not_do: The same identification move (randomised replacement of the inter-agent message, pre-registered equivalence margins) applied to a latent KV channel in released latent-communication systems; it audits whether a channel transmits example-specific information ('A large cache effect need not be a pairing effect'), never a text brief or return in orchestrator-executor delegation, never against a single-agent baseline at matched tool budget, never two channels with a Shapley split of a loss, and never a pre/post-cutoff difference-in-differences. It is the proof that the design works on a MAS channel, which is why the import is cheap now.

papers.title: Learning What to Skip: Counterfactual Credit Assignment for Efficient Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
papers.trick: Treat omitting a workflow component (planner, verifier, summariser) as a counterfactual: run controlled skip interventions, learn per-component safety models from the revealed consequences, and skip components whose conditional value is low, cutting tokens at matched or better accuracy.
papers.did_not_do: Randomised exclusion of whole components for the purpose of learning a skip policy; the unit is the component, not the message content that crosses a boundary, the comparison is full workflow versus skipped workflow rather than delegated system versus single agent at matched budget, there is no Shapley split, no interaction term, no post-cutoff memory-is-wrong condition, and no claim about the identifiability of 'responsible agent' labels. Third: AgenTracer 2509.03312 uses 'counterfactual replay and programmed fault injection' to manufacture step labels for training a tracer, on failed runs only, never on the handoff messages and never at matched budgets. Fourth: A2P 2509.10401 has the LLM 'simulate the subsequent trajectory' of a corrective intervention in one inference pass, a predicted counterfactual, not a run one. Fifth: SHARP 2602.08335 and 2511.10687 use Shapley credit over agents as an RL reward, estimated or theoretical, never measured by running coalitions. Sixth: 2607.22448 attributes omission per pipeline layer with injected deterministic faults and states that its 'confounded model comparisons, and heuristic behavioral labels do not measure production prevalence or causal architectural effects'. Seventh: 2611.16526 (card) has the unmatched grid and the four judged rates; 2611.13254 (card) has the reach table that 'is not a measured intervention'. Pre-window precedents with their tricks: Who&When 2505.00212 (human 'responsible agent' and 'decisive step' labels; best automated attribution 53.5% agent, 14.2% step); MAST 2503.13657 (14-mode failure taxonomy from 150 hand-read traces).

nearest.verdict: Not made. The randomised-replacement audit of an inter-agent channel exists for latent KV relays (2608.04893), counterfactual omission of components exists as a skip-policy learner (2609.30734), counterfactual replay exists as a label factory for trace-reading judges (2509.03312) and as a predicted counterfactual (2509.10401), Shapley credit over agents exists as an RL reward (2602.08335, 2511.10687), and the delegation loss exists as an unmatched grid with judged rates (2611.16526); no fetched source randomises the brief and the return of an orchestrator-executor handoff at matched budget and instruction, splits a delegation loss between the two messages, or tests whether a single responsible unit exists where every coalition was run (22 field-word hits, 54 neighbour-word hits, 15 lane-word hits). It is not a rename of 2608.04893 because the object (text messages in same-model delegation against a single-agent baseline) and the quantity (a Shapley split of a loss plus the matched DiD, not a pairing-effect test) differ, and not a rename of the Who&When line because that line labels by reading and this import says reading identifies nothing.

reason_for_pick: S10 is the lane's live shape this week through card 2611.16526 (same-model delegation loses 9-11 points post-cutoff in arms unmatched in budget and instruction, with the loss attributed by judged rates) and card 2611.13254 (control reach and responsible-agent labels as trace readings, 'not a measured intervention'); S10xF8 is a suggested first pair in fields.yaml never logged, and S10 has never been imported into. F8 is the field whose whole subject is that credit read off a record is unidentified without an assignment the record did not choose, which is the gap both cards state in their own words; the two-player Shapley identity and the 2 x 2 factorial are checkable by hand, the datasets are public and numeric, and 2608.04893 showed the replacement audit works on a MAS channel, so the probe is a harness with a budget counter and two switches. Pairs with the S3 and S8 rows of the W45-W46 block.

scorecard.target_value: In print: 2611.16526 ('may contribute to the observed lower accuracy', sec. 5.3; 'targeted mechanisms for communicating evidence and resolving conflicts rather than simple prompt interventions', sec. 6; 'Passing complete executor traces ... would undermine the context-saving benefits', sec. 7; tokens never counted); 2611.13254 ('"Would have reached" is a judgment about the trace ... It is not a measured intervention', sec. 5.1; 45% of a public split scored on harness-generated answers attributed to agents); 2610.17747 (simple cue predictors match or beat GPT-4.1 as attribution judges); 2604.22708 (full traces raise attribution accuracy by up to 76%, so the labels depend on what the judge is shown). Who pays: every team deploying orchestrator-subagent systems and choosing a return schema; the owners of attribution benchmarks whose labels are trained on.

scorecard.density_and_ownership: The failure-attribution line is dense: 54 arXiv hits for 'failure attribution' with multi-agent words, about two a week since 2026-05, and 22 for the field words with credit or blame; nearly all are trace-reading judges, learned attributers or benchmarks of them (BLADE, DCFA, CHIEF, SOAP, DuoTrace, Who&When Pro, TraceElephant), and their own audit (2610.17747) says the judges follow cues. Occupied: randomised replacement of a latent KV channel (2608.04893); skip interventions on components (2609.30734); counterfactual replay as a label factory (2509.03312) and as a predicted counterfactual (2509.10401); Shapley credit over agents as reward (2602.08335, 2511.10687); the unmatched delegation grid with judged rates (2611.16526); per-layer omission attribution with injected faults (2607.22448). Unoccupied in every fetched source: randomising the brief and the return of a text handoff at matched budget and instruction against a single agent; the Shapley split of a delegation loss between the two messages with the interaction; the matched pre/post-cutoff DiD; and the share of lost items with no single responsible unit. Natural first movers: the 2611.16526 authors (they hold the harness and the datasets; code release unknown) and the 2608.04893 authors (they hold the audit design); the re-open test is asking them. Race window: 2611.16526 is three days old; a matched-budget follow-up from its authors within two to three months is the live threat against an 11-day probe on public data; window at least 2x time-to-result holds for the probe, not for a longer study. Solo position: public sources, open model, about 30 GPU-hours and $1,100; proper-shaped solo, golden only if an attribution benchmark owner adopts the intervention label.
scorecard.why_now: 2611.16526 (2026-11-12) published the same-model delegation grid with a 9-11 point post-cutoff loss, arms unmatched in budget (Table 7) and instruction (Table 8), and four judged rates offered as attribution; 2611.13254 (2026-11-09) wrote in print that control reach and responsible-agent labels are trace readings and not measured interventions, and found 45% of a public attribution split scored on harness-generated answers; 2610.17747 (2026-10-13) showed attribution judges follow surface cues; 2608.04893 (2026-08) established the randomised-replacement audit of a MAS channel with pre-registered equivalence margins, so the design is standard and the probe is a harness with a budget counter and two switches; pre/post-cutoff paired datasets (2605.28721, 2611.16526) give a memory-is-wrong condition that makes the brief channel's folded-in guess detectable.
scorecard.register_and_what_it_is_not: Measurement register: a randomised factorial with a two-player Shapley split and a difference-in-differences, a mechanism (a rewritten brief folds a wrong guess into the executor's task; an unmatched instruction converts wrong memory into skipped searches) and three consequences (match budgets before claiming a boundary effect; pick return fields by marginal contribution per token; add an intervention-identified label to attribution benchmarks). It is not a new orchestrator, not a learned or prompted attributer, not a trace-reading judge, not an RL credit method, and not a variance split (CL-W43-14, CL-W45-08): the quantities are mean contrasts that survive temperature 0.

title: A greedy decode is a hidden fixed facet: the union-versus-best 'forgetting' gap of a GRPO run (Agentic-OPD's 4,553 against 2,808; Temporal Sampling's 6.4-56.1%) is a checkpoint-by-problem table read once per cell, so the forgetting component is unidentified until some checkpoints are decoded $m$ times at the RL sampling temperature and the gap is split into probability drops, coin-flip cells and argmax flips
abstract: In generalizability theory a score observed once per cell of a crossed design cannot separate the highest-order interaction from error, and a facet observed under one condition for every cell is 'hidden and fixed': its variance is absorbed into the component it sits under and inflates it (Brennan 2000). In performance assessment the person-by-task-by-occasion interaction, the occasion-specific flip of one task's outcome, was 59% of total variance while the occasion main effect was 1% (Shavelson, Gao and Baxter 1993). Carried into L2, that says the 'forgotten problems' of a GRPO run are cells of a checkpoint-by-problem table, each read by one greedy decode (Agentic-OPD 2611.12799 sec. 2: 'We use greedy decoding for all checkpoint evaluations'; Temporal Sampling 2505.20196 sec. 2.2: 'To minimize variability ... we employ greedy sampling'), so the decoding draw is a hidden fixed facet and the measured gap mixes three things the policy's owner would act on differently: a problem whose success probability fell (forgetting, a property of the policy), a problem whose success probability sits near one half at every checkpoint and whose single decode lands on either side (a coin flip, a property of the protocol), and a near-tied argmax that flips under five RL steps (argmax churn, a property of the greedy protocol on a near-deterministic policy). Pre-registered: on an own Search-R1-recipe GRPO run at 3B, with $m = 8$ draws per (checkpoint, problem) at the RL sampling temperature, at least half of the greedy gap set has a best-checkpoint success probability between 0.2 and 0.8 and at most a fifth is a strict drop (above 0.8 at some earlier checkpoint, below 0.2 at the best); if strict drops are at least half the gap, forgetting within one run is a real, large, problem-specific property and the greedy ruler stands.

sentences: A crossed design observes each object under every condition of every facet and reports one variance component per facet and per interaction; in Brennan's performance-assessment example (persons $p$ by tasks $t$ by raters $r$) the components are 'the variance over p, t, and r of single person-task-rater scores' and the last is 'a residual VC that includes the triple-order interaction and all other unexplained sources of variation', so with one observation per cell the highest-order interaction and the unexplained error are one number (Brennan, Applied Psychological Measurement 24(4), 2000, pp. 339-353); the decision study then divides each component by the number of conditions of the facets it contains, 'Relative error variance is the sum of the D study VCs that include the index p and at least one other index', and 'A generalizability coefficient is the ratio of universe score variance to itself plus relative error variance'.

A facet observed under a single condition for every cell does not disappear from the variance, it is absorbed: 'When all persons respond to the same single task, the single task is effectively hidden and fixed for all persons', which 'leads to $\sigma^2(pt)$ being included with $\sigma^2(p)$' and inflates the coefficient (Brennan 2000); and the occasion facet, 'all possible occasions on which a decision maker would be equally willing to accept a score', is the retest facet, 'Sampling variability due to occasions corresponds to the classical notion of retest reliability' (Shavelson, Gao and Baxter, CSE Technical Report 361, 1993, pp. 2, 4); in their person by rater by task by occasion science assessment 'The major source of measurement error was due to the person x task x occasion interaction' at about 59% of total variance, against about 1% for the occasion main effect and about 4% for the residual (pp. 12-13), and in the simpler person by item design the interaction 'is confounded with other disturbances not included in the p x i design, and random error' (p. 16).

Where to spend replicates: Neyman (optimum) allocation minimises the variance of a stratified mean under the cost constraint $\sum_{h} c_h n_h = C_0$, 'where $C_0$ is the overall budget available and $c_h$ the average survey cost for an individual in stratum $h$', by $n^{opt}_h = \frac{N_h S_h}{\sqrt{c_h}} \frac{C_0}{\sum_{h} N_h S_h \sqrt{c_h}}$ with $N_h$ the stratum size and $S_h$ its within-stratum standard deviation (Osier, Survey data in Economics and Finance, sec. 3.3.3, eq. 3.14, citing Cochran 1977), so a stratum with zero within-stratum spread gets no replicates and the gain over equal allocation is largest when the $S_h$ differ most, which for Bernoulli cells with $S_h = \sqrt{p_h(1-p_h)}$ between 0 and 0.5 is the usual case; and metrology's nested time design, 'J short-term measurements are replicated on K days and the entire operation is then replicated over L runs', with $s_1$ 'with (J-1) degrees of freedom for short-term errors', $s_2$ 'with (K-1) degrees of freedom for day-to-day errors' and $s_3$ 'with (L-1) degrees of freedom for very long-term errors' (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook sec. 2.5.3.1.1), gives the three time scales a replicate can live on: the draw, the checkpoint, the training run.

import_sentence: In experimental design and generalizability theory, 'did this unit really change between occasions, or did I read one noisy outcome each time' is answered by a crossed design that treats the unit (problem), the occasion (checkpoint) and the replicate (decoding draw) each as a facet, estimates one variance component per facet and interaction, notes that one observation per cell leaves the occasion-by-unit interaction confounded with the replicate residual and that a facet held at one condition everywhere (one greedy decode) is a hidden fixed facet whose variance is absorbed into the interaction it sits under, and spends replicates by Neyman's rule on the cells with the largest within-cell spread; carried into L2, that says the 'forgotten problems' of a GRPO run, Agentic-OPD's $|U_{\geq 1} \setminus Q_{\mathrm{best}}|$ (4,553 solved by at least three of 100 checkpoints against 2,808 by the final one, HotpotQA, Qwen2.5-3B, 2611.12799 sec. 2) and Temporal Sampling's $P_{\mathrm{TFS}}$ (6.4% to 56.1% of final errors once solved, 2505.20196 sec. 2.2), are checkpoint-by-problem cells read by one greedy decode each, so the forgetting component of a run is unidentified until some checkpoints are decoded $m$ times at the RL sampling temperature and the greedy gap is split into probability drops (the policy's), coin-flip cells (the protocol's) and argmax flips of a near-deterministic policy (the greedy protocol's), with the draws allocated to the cells whose first draws disagree.

predicts.statement: Setup: one GRPO run under the Search-R1 recipe (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, HotpotQA, Wikipedia retriever, 4 turns, the recipe Agentic-OPD follows), $n = 30$ checkpoints saved every 10 steps over 300 steps, a fixed validation set of $N = 1{,}000$ problems $x$. Outcomes: $Y^{g}_{ix} \in \{0,1\}$ is the greedy decode of checkpoint $i$ on $x$ (the paper's $C_{T_i}(x)$); $Y_{ixd} \in \{0,1\}$ is draw $d = 1..m$ of checkpoint $i$ on $x$ at the RL rollout temperature ($T = 1.0$, the recipe's), $m = 8$, on a subset of $n_s = 10$ checkpoints (every 30 steps, plus the best-validation and final ones); $\hat p_{ix} = \frac{1}{m}\sum_d Y_{ixd}$. Greedy sets as in the paper: $Q_i = \{x : Y^g_{ix} = 1\}$, $U_{\geq 1} = \bigcup_i Q_i$, gap set $G = U_{\geq 1} \setminus Q_{\mathrm{best}}$, and $P_{\mathrm{TFS}} = |U_{\geq 1} \setminus Q_n| / N$. Model for the probability table: $$\hat p_{ix} = \mu + \alpha_i + \beta_x + \gamma_{ix} + e_{ix},$$ with $\alpha_i$ the checkpoint main effect (the learning curve), $\beta_x$ the problem main effect (difficulty), $\gamma_{ix}$ the checkpoint-by-problem interaction (problem-specific learning and forgetting, the only term that is 'forgetting' as a property of the policy) and $e_{ix}$ the binomial draw error with known variance $\hat p_{ix}(1-\hat p_{ix})/m$; components $\sigma^2_c, \sigma^2_x, \sigma^2_{cx}$ by two-way ANOVA with the binomial term subtracted from the residual mean square (the correction 2611.16315 applies to its item means), intervals by a problem-cluster bootstrap. Cell classes at the best checkpoint: settled-solved ($\hat p_{\mathrm{best},x} \geq 0.8$), coin-flip ($0.2 < \hat p_{\mathrm{best},x} < 0.8$), settled-failed ($\leq 0.2$); strict drop: $\max_i \hat p_{ix} \geq 0.8$ and $\hat p_{\mathrm{best},x} \leq 0.2$. P1 (composition of the greedy gap): among $x \in G$, the coin-flip share is at least 0.5 and the strict-drop share at most 0.2. P2 (reliability of one draw): the intraclass correlation of draws within cells, $\rho_1 = \mathrm{Var}(p_{ix}) / [\mathrm{Var}(p_{ix}) + \mathbb{E}\,p_{ix}(1-p_{ix})]$ over the 10 x 1,000 cells, lies between 0.5 and 0.8, so a single draw carries 20-50% noise variance per cell (against 9% for the continuous Fermi task of 2611.16315), and the D-study count of draws for $\rho_m = m\rho_1/(1 + (m-1)\rho_1) \geq 0.9$ is $m \geq 3$ to $9$. P3 (persistence, from the greedy table alone): among $x \in G$, the share whose sequence $(Y^g_{1x}, \ldots, Y^g_{nx})$ has at least three switches (flickering) is at least 0.6, and the switch count is not below the independent-Bernoulli value at the same marginal, $2 (n-1)\, \bar Y_x (1 - \bar Y_x)$, for more than a third of them; a lost-for-good problem (one switch, down) is under 0.15 of $G$. P4 (Gate 0 control, temperature 0): re-decoding one checkpoint greedily under three batch compositions changes $Y^g_{ix}$ on under 3% of problems; above 5% the greedy sets themselves carry a serving component (2602.07150) and the paper's gap includes it. Consequence written now: the recoverable target of a consolidation stage is the strict-drop count, not $|G|$; Agentic-OPD's own best case (60 recovered, 45 lost, net 15 of 2,000, sec. 4.3) is the churn P1 predicts when teachers are chosen by set cover on coin-flip cells.
predicts.expected: Judgment, not evidence: probability 0.55 that P1 holds (coin-flip share at least 0.5, strict drops at most 0.2); 0.25 that strict drops are between 0.2 and 0.5; 0.2 that strict drops are at least 0.5. Probability 0.5 for P2's band; 0.25 that $\rho_1 > 0.8$ (the RL policy near-deterministic at $T = 1$, entropy collapse), 0.25 that $\rho_1 < 0.5$. Probability 0.65 for P3; 0.8 for P4's under-3% reading. Expected mechanism: GRPO on a 3B policy over 4-turn retrieval episodes leaves a wide band of problems at intermediate success probability (the paper's own LAD filter exists because $G$-sample rates on training problems are fractional, eq. 10); five RL steps move the argmax at near-tied tokens without moving the probability much, so the greedy table flickers on exactly the coin-flip problems; the first greedy success puts such a problem into $U_{\geq 1}$ within a few checkpoints ($1 - (1-p)^{n}$ with $n = 100$ and any $p \geq 0.05$ exceeds 0.99 under independence; under the positive correlation of adjacent checkpoints the count is smaller but the ordering is the same), and the final greedy decode lands on the failed side with probability near $1 - p$, so the union-versus-final gap is large with no change in any problem's probability. Temporal Sampling's own evidence cuts the other way and is weighed: its Pass@k|t gain of 4-19 points over Pass@k on the final checkpoint (8 checkpoints, 64 samples at $T = 0.6$) requires some $r_{i,j}$ to exceed the final checkpoint's on some problems, which is nonzero $\sigma^2_{cx}$ in probability space on math; that is why the strict-drop share is pre-registered at up to 0.2 and not at zero.
predicts.field_assumes: The lane reads the greedy gap as capability lost: Agentic-OPD calls it 'forgotten agent capabilities', builds its teacher scheduler on the greedy sets ($Q_i, P_t, \Delta_{i,t}$, eqs. 4-9) and concedes only that 'measuring how much of the historical task coverage can be reliably recovered' is a 'useful next step' (sec. 5); Temporal Sampling defines $P_{\mathrm{TFS}}$ from greedy decodes and chooses greedy to remove noise, 'To minimize variability arising from different sampling methods during evaluation, we employ greedy sampling' (sec. 2.2), then describes the table it gets, 'the model oscillates between correct and incorrect answers across checkpoints' (Figure 3), as forgetting dynamics rather than as the draw facet it fixed; neither paper decodes any checkpoint twice for the forgetting measurement, estimates a per-cell success probability on the forgetting set, or reports a noise floor, and Agentic-OPD's only robustness device is $U_{\geq k}$ for $k = 2, 3$. Generalizability theory's assumption is the reverse (Brennan 2000): a facet held at one condition is hidden, not removed, and its variance is read as the interaction above it; the replicate is what identifies the interaction.
predicts.belief_changing: If P1 holds, 'temporal forgetting' and the union-versus-best gap are protocol numbers until a draw floor is reported: every checkpoint-consolidation or temporal-sampling paper must report $\rho_1$ and $m$ beside its forgetting score, HCN-style schedulers must select teachers on $\hat p$ differences with a replicate rule rather than on greedy set cover, and the recoverable target of consolidation is a fifth of the headline (a lane-wide protocol change, Gate 3). If strict drops are at least half of $G$, forgetting within one RL run is a large problem-specific property of the policy, the greedy ruler over-counts by under a factor of two, and the import is a footnote that licenses it. If $\rho_1 > 0.8$ with most cells settled, the policy at $T = 1$ is near-deterministic, the draw facet is empty by the policy's own entropy, and the greedy gap is argmax churn under parameter updates: then P3's persistence statistics are the forgetting measurement, Temporal Sampling at $T > 0$ has nothing to recover that one checkpoint's sampling would not, and the belief that changes is which facet carries the dice (the optimiser's step, not the sampler).

identifiability: Random given: fixed task set, fixed retriever index and retrieval function (the Search-R1 Wikipedia retriever returns the same passages for the same query, so the environment is deterministic given the action sequence), fixed checkpoint weights, fixed prompt and turn cap, fixed serving stack. Whose temperature: at temperature 0 the draw facet is zero by construction on this environment, up to the serving stack's batch-dependent arithmetic (2602.07150; P4 measures it), so a greedy solved set is a deterministic function of (checkpoint, protocol) and 'forgetting' read from it is the checkpoint-by-problem interaction of the argmax path: a property of the policy's argmax, which is a discontinuous functional of the weights that flips at near-tied tokens under five RL steps, hence a property of the (policy, greedy protocol) pair and not of the success probability any consumer deploys at. At the RL rollout temperature ($T = 1.0$; the paper's own test-time settings are $T = 1.0$ for Tool-use and $T = 0.7$ for the AgentGym domains) the per-cell success probability $p_{ix}$ is a property of the policy, the draw residual $p_{ix}(1-p_{ix})$ is the protocol's and is known from $p_{ix}$ itself (Bernoulli), and the interaction $\gamma_{ix}$ is the quantity whose change across $i$ is forgetting. The record therefore reports components at the stated temperature and separately the temperature-0 repeatability; the greedy facet is a hidden fixed facet in Brennan's sense, so under greedy the term $\sigma^2_{cx}$ absorbs the draw-by-cell variance and is read as inflated, not as zero. A seed is not a state of the world: $m$ draws at one checkpoint are exchangeable by construction when inputs are identical; the 100 checkpoints are not exchangeable (they are a trajectory), so the interaction is estimated as a variance component but its persistence is read from the ordered sequence (P3), and the independent-Bernoulli switch count is a reference, not a null the data must obey. Protocol choices reported with sensitivity rows: $m \in \{4, 8, 16\}$ on a 200-problem subset; thresholds 0.2 / 0.8 and 0.3 / 0.7; the number of checkpoints $n$ (the gap grows with $n$ under the coin-flip account and saturates under the drop account, which is itself a diagnostic). Judge versus verifier: the outcome is exact match against the reference string, a verifier, never a judge. Property of what: $\sigma^2_x$ belongs to the validation set and policy family, $\sigma^2_c$ to the run, $\sigma^2_{cx}$ to the run's trajectory on this set, $\mathbb{E}\,p(1-p)$ to the policy's entropy under the stated sampler; shares are reported per run with the components, not shares alone.

probe.design: Step 0 (no training; about 6 GPU-hours, 2 days): with the Search-R1 harness and a public 3B instruct policy (a released Search-R1 checkpoint if one is available on the Hub at run time, else Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct untrained), on 500 HotpotQA validation problems: (a) greedy decode under three batch compositions for the temperature-0 repeatability (P4); (b) $m = 8$ draws at $T = 1.0$ for the coin-flip share $f$ of cells and $\rho_1$ for one checkpoint; (c) arithmetic: the expected union-versus-final gap over $n = 100$ checkpoints under a stationary policy with the measured $\hat p$ distribution, as an independence upper reference and a fully-correlated lower reference, to bracket where 4,553 against 2,808 sits with no forgetting at all. Step 1 (the G-study; the main cost): one GRPO run under the Search-R1 recipe, Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct on HotpotQA, 300 steps, checkpoint every 10 steps ($n = 30$), on 8 GPUs; greedy decode of all 30 checkpoints on 1,000 validation problems (30,000 four-turn episodes) for the greedy table, $G$, $P_{\mathrm{TFS}}$ and P3; $m = 8$ draws at $T = 1.0$ on 10 checkpoints x 1,000 problems (80,000 episodes) for $\hat p_{ix}$, the components, P1 and P2; Neyman row: re-run the draw stage two-stage (4 draws everywhere, 4 more only where the first 4 disagree) and report the draw count saved at equal classification of cells, with $m_{ix} \propto \sqrt{\hat p_{ix}(1-\hat p_{ix})}$ as the reference allocation. Step 2 (optional, about 15 GPU-hours): the same decode design on the 8 checkpoints of a Temporal-Sampling-style math GRPO run at 1.5B (DeepScaleR-4k subset, MATH-500 and OlympiadBench), to read the strict-drop share where Temporal Sampling's 4-19 point Pass@k|t gain says $\sigma^2_{cx} > 0$. Cheaper fallback for step 1: Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct (about half the cost) or 500 validation problems; the claim is about the ruler, not the model size. Deliverable: a one-page variance-component card for one RL run (components, $\rho_1$, D-study curve of $\rho_m$, gap composition, persistence histogram) and the two-stage replicate rule as a table any forgetting paper can adopt.
probe.dollars: about $350 at H100 on-demand rates for steps 0-1 (training about 60-100 GPU-hours, judgment: the paper gives no figure for its 500-step run on 8 A800s; decoding about 110,000 four-turn episodes at 3B with vLLM, about 40-70 GPU-hours); about $40 more for step 2; the 1.5B fallback is about $180
probe.days: 12 days: 2 for step 0, 2 of harness work, 3 of training and decoding, 3 of analysis, 2 for step 2
probe.kills_if: Dead as the claim 'the greedy gap is mostly protocol' if the strict-drop share of $G$ is at least 0.5 with the bootstrap interval's lower end above 0.35 at $m = 8$, $T = 1.0$: forgetting within one run is then a real problem-specific property and the greedy ruler over-counts by under 2x, a footnote licensing it. Dead as a ruler if at least 90% of the 10,000 cells have $\hat p_{ix} \in \{0, 1\}$ at $m = 8$ (policy near-deterministic at the RL temperature): the draw facet is empty by the policy's entropy, and the record closes with P3's persistence statistics as the result. Dead at Gate 0 for the greedy sets themselves if P4's temperature-0 disagreement exceeds 5% of problems: then the published greedy tables contain a serving component and the paper's gap cannot be reproduced on another server. Recorded either way: the components, $\rho_1$, the gap composition and the switch-count histogram, each of which changes one stated belief above.

consumers.class: Evaluation infrastructure and checkpoint-selection tooling in L1 (best-of-run selection, per-checkpoint validation in RL frameworks, the robot pass@k-across-checkpoints line of 2611.01565)

papers.title: Temporal Sampling for Forgotten Reasoning in LLMs
papers.trick: Count the questions some saved checkpoint of an RL or SFT run answered correctly that the final checkpoint gets wrong (the Temporal Forgetting Score, 6.4-56.1% of final errors on Qwen2.5 1.5B-7B math runs), then at test time spread the $k$ samples round-robin over several checkpoints, which raises Pass@k by 4-19 points because the per-checkpoint success rates $r_{i,j}$ differ across checkpoints on the same problem.
papers.did_not_do: Its forgetting score is one greedy decode per (checkpoint, question): 'To minimize variability arising from different sampling methods during evaluation, we employ greedy sampling' (sec. 2.2), 8 checkpoints per run; it then reads the resulting table as dynamics, 'Questions exhibits alternating Improve and Forget events frequently during training, which means the model oscillates between correct and incorrect answers across checkpoints' (Figure 3), without decoding any checkpoint twice, estimating a per-cell probability for the forgetting set, or stating a noise floor. It holds the data to do so for its method ($r_{i,j}$ from 64 samples at $T = 0.6$ on 8 checkpoints, sec. 3) and never applies it to $P_{\mathrm{TFS}}$: no strict-drop share, no coin-flip share, no persistence statistic, and its limitations (App. B) name only domains and training frameworks. Math only; no agent loop.

papers.title: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
papers.trick: Keep every checkpoint of a GRPO run, mark which validation problems each one solves by one greedy decode, show the union over checkpoints (4,553 by at least three of 100 checkpoints) far exceeds the final checkpoint's set (2,808), then distill the best checkpoint toward whichever earlier checkpoint covers most of its current greedy failures, on failed rollouts only.
papers.did_not_do: 'We use greedy decoding for all checkpoint evaluations' (sec. 2); no checkpoint is decoded twice, no per-problem success probability is estimated on the validation set, the only robustness device is $U_{\geq k}$ for $k = 2, 3$ ('Raising $k$ drops the tasks only a single checkpoint ever solved'), bootstrap intervals appear only for SciWorld (App. A.2), and the paper concedes that 'measuring how much of the historical task coverage can be reliably recovered' is a 'useful next step' (sec. 5); its $G$-sample rates exist only on training problems and only to admit them to the loss (eq. 10). Its best measured recovery, 60 recovered and 45 lost for net 15 of 2,000 (sec. 4.3), is reported as consolidation, not compared with the churn of re-decoding. Third: 2611.16315 (card) has the exact decomposition and $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ arithmetic for a continuous Fermi task with no checkpoint facet (item 0.906, draw 0.094 given the model). Fourth: 2611.01565 measures closed-loop pass@k across robot pretraining checkpoints with repeated rollouts and finds 'pass@k peaks at different checkpoints', the right measurement for a different question (coverage versus reliability for post-training), with no forgetting set and no variance components. Pre-window precedents with their tricks: G-theory variance components for agent scores with no checkpoint or draw-within-checkpoint facet (2608.11323: agent-by-task 7-23%; 2610.00651: within-cell term fixed at $\pi^2/3$ because repeats are rare; the W43 S6xF1 and S8xF1 records); temperature-0 variance as serving arithmetic (2602.07150).

nearest.verdict: Not made. Temporal Sampling and Agentic-OPD both measure forgetting across checkpoints by one greedy decode per cell and both state the choice; the first holds per-checkpoint sampled rates for its method and never turns them on its forgetting score; the second concedes the reliability question as future work. The variance-components machinery is in print for agent scores (W43 records) and for a continuous task with a draw facet (2611.16315), never with a checkpoint facet or on a forgetting set; 2611.01565 samples across checkpoints in robotics for coverage, not forgetting. 1 + 6 + 10 API hits, none with the checkpoint x problem x draw design. Not a rename of 'single decodes are noisy' (pass@k folklore): the content is the hidden-fixed-facet reading of greedy, the three-way split of the gap set with pre-registered shares, the persistence statistic as the forgetting measurement when the draw facet is empty, and the two-stage Neyman replicate rule; not a repeat of S6xF1 (cost), S8xF1 (effort-by-task) or S7xF3 (runs per leaderboard cell): the unit here is the (checkpoint, problem) cell inside one training run.

reason_for_pick: S12 (learning from noisy single outcomes) is this week's live shape through card 2611.12799, whose load-bearing assumption is that a greedy single decode per (checkpoint, problem) marks a capability and whose own recovery accounting (60 gained, 45 lost) looks like churn; F1 is in Jacob's evaluable set and its agent-score imports (S6xF1, S8xF1, W43) left the within-run checkpoint facet untouched. Brennan's hidden-fixed-facet rule names exactly what greedy decoding does to the draw facet, and 2611.16315 (carded this week) supplies the same decomposition on a continuous task with the binomial correction and the $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ arithmetic, so the import is a design (checkpoint x problem x draw) with a known fitting recipe and a sub-GPU-week probe on a public RL recipe.

scorecard.density_and_ownership: Checkpoint-ensembling and temporal-forgetting for LLM RL: about one paper a month in the API window (Temporal Sampling 2025-05, GTR-Turbo 2025-12, 2602.03073, 2509.12235, Agentic-OPD 2026-11), none with a replicate on the forgetting set. Unoccupied in every fetched source: a per-cell success probability on the forgetting set, the three-way split of the gap (drop / coin flip / argmax flip) with a reported draw floor, the persistence statistic as the forgetting measurement under an empty draw facet, and a replicate-allocation rule for checkpoint tables. Natural first movers: the Temporal Sampling authors (they hold $r_{i,j}$ for 8 checkpoints and could compute the split today) and the Agentic-OPD authors (they hold 100 checkpoints); the re-open test is asking them. Race window: a 12-day probe on a public recipe against about one relevant paper a month; proper-shaped from the solo position.

scorecard.register_and_what_it_is_not: Measurement register: a variance-component card for one RL run (checkpoint, problem, interaction, draw), a reliability coefficient for the greedy solved set, a three-way split of the forgetting gap with pre-registered shares, and a replicate rule; mechanism (five RL steps flip near-tied argmaxes without moving probabilities) and consequence (what a consolidation stage can recover; how many draws a checkpoint table needs). It is not a new consolidation recipe, not a critique of OPD, not a run-to-run variance study of agent scores (CL-W43-14, CL-W44-07) and not the cost (S6xF1) or effort (S8xF1) imports: the unit is the (checkpoint, problem) cell inside one training run and the question is which facet carries the dice.

title: A lesson is a shipped unit: fit the hazard of memory-induced failure against a lesson's use-age (falling, flat or rising) with lesson frailty separated, because admission probes (burn-in), evidence-linked descent at every use (per-use inspection) and certificate restarts or retirement (scheduled replacement) are the three maintenance policies of reliability engineering and the shape, measured nowhere in the fetched lane, decides which one pays
abstract: In reliability engineering a population of new units does not fail at one rate: the hazard (the chance of failing in the next instant given survival so far) is high and falling at first (early failures from defective units), flat for a long middle (random failures at the intrinsic rate) and rising at the end (wear-out); for a fleet or a repairable system the same shape is fitted as a power law in age, $M(t) = a t^{b}$ expected failures by age $t$ with rate $m(t) = a b\, t^{b-1}$, and the shape, not the level, picks the policy: a falling rate calls for acceptance tests and burn-in before shipment, a flat rate makes burn-in and overhaul useless ('old parts are assumed to be as good as new parts') so only redesign helps, a rising rate calls for scheduled replacement (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook 8.1.2.4, 8.1.7.2, 8.1.9.1-2; PTC Windchill Weibull guide). Carried into L4, that says a lesson distilled from one success- or failure-labelled trajectory (S12: a unit of unknown quality, its defect a false prior from a lucky success or an unlucky failure) is a shipped unit whose age is its retrieval count $u$ and whose failure is a memory-induced failure (WikiTrace 2611.14320: the agent fails a task it solves with the lesson withheld), that the lifecycle designs now in print are the three maintenance policies in disguise, each presupposing a hazard shape it never measured: FGSE 2611.14326's admission probes and SkillForge 2610.09832's pre-retirement are burn-in (defects at birth, falling hazard); WikiTrace's evidence-linked descent at every use and REM 2610.27377's in-loop gate are per-use inspection (flat hazard, harm a per-use draw); 2610.17544's certificate restarts, TrackRL 2610.25126's retirement and Library Drift 2605.19576's capacity bound are scheduled replacement (rising hazard, by fact edits, internalization or crowding); and TrackRL's 'protected incubation' bets the opposite sign to burn-in. The ruler: per (lesson, use) pair, the paired harm $\hat\delta_{\ell u}$ from $n$ runs with the retrieved set and $n$ with the lesson withheld (CoReMem 2611.17316's with/without contrast at lesson grain; TrackRL's random withholding), read by use-age bin with a lesson random effect (frailty) and a store-size covariate (crowding), against a frozen-store arm in which the shape is flat by construction. Pre-registered: the hazard rises with use-age and the rise is absorbed by store size (crowding at lesson grain; judgment 0.4), with strong frailty (a fifth of lessons carry over half the harm; 0.6); then burn-in with $k$ probes catches a lesson of per-use harm $p$ with probability $1-(1-p)^{k}$, which for FGSE's probe count is the predicted leakage behind its 3.6% harmful commits, and the right design is a capacity or age bound, not more probe types. Probe: about 30 GPU-hours on ALFWorld with WikiTrace's released insight store, 9 days, solo.

sentences: A population of new units does not fail at one rate. The failure rate over the life of a product is a bathtub: an early failure period 'characterized by a high but rapidly decreasing failure rate', also 'referred to as Infant Mortality', that 'typically lasts several weeks to a few months'; then 'the failure rate levels off and remains roughly constant' through 'the Intrinsic Failure Period', whose level 'is called the Intrinsic Failure Rate'; then a wear-out period in which 'the failure rate begins to increase as materials wear out and degradation failures occur at an ever increasing rate' (NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook sec. 8.1.2.4).

For a repairable system or a fleet the same shape is fitted as a power law in age: expected failures by age $t$ are $M(t) = a t^{b}$ and the rate of occurrence of failures is $m(t) = a b\, t^{b-1}$, with $a > 0$ a scale and $b$ the shape; 'when $b = 1$ ... the model reduces to the HPP constant repair rate model' $m(t) = \lambda$; $0 < b < 1$ is a falling rate, which in a test-analyze-and-fix program is read as reliability growth ('improvement occurs when $0 < \beta < 1$', $\beta = 1 - b$ the Duane slope, read off a log-log plot of cumulative failures per unit age against age; 'when an improvement test ends, the MTBF stays constant at its last achieved value'), and $b > 1$ is a rising rate, deterioration (NIST/SEMATECH secs. 8.1.7.1, 8.1.7.2, 8.1.9.1, 8.1.9.2).

The shape, not the level, picks the policy. With a Weibull shape under 1 'newer parts are more likely to fail', so 'manufacturers provide production acceptance tests, "burn-in" and environmental stress screenings' and 'overhaul of parts experiencing high infant mortality is generally not appropriate'; at shape 1 'the failure rate is constant or independent of time', 'old parts are assumed to be as good as new parts, overhaul is generally not appropriate' and 'the only way to increase reliability for components or systems that experience random failures is by redesigning them'; above 1 the system 'may be improved by optimizing the preventative maintenance schedule' and 'overhauls or part replacements at low B-lives may be cost effective' (PTC Windchill Quality Solutions, 'Understanding Weibull Analysis', following Abernethy's handbook).
sources: https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/toolaids/pff/apr.pdf — NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, ch. 8 'Assessing Product Reliability' as one PDF; sec. 8.1.2.4 'Bathtub curve' (early failure / infant mortality, intrinsic failure period, wear-out), secs. 8.1.7.1-8.1.7.2 (HPP; NHPP power law, $b$ above, equal to and below 1) (fetched 2026-11-15; the HTML page apr124.htm was blocked by the fetch permission and is cited through the chapter PDF)

https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/section1/apr191.htm — sec. 8.1.9.1 'NHPP power law' for reliability growth: $M(t) = a t^{b}$, $m(t) = a b t^{b-1}$, $\beta = 1 - b$, improvement when $0 < \beta < 1$, MTBF constant after the test ends (fetched 2026-11-15)
https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/apr/section1/apr192.htm — sec. 8.1.9.2 'Duane plots': log-log plot of $t_i / i$ against $t_i$; slope between 0.3 and 0.6 in practice (fetched 2026-11-15)

https://support.ptc.com/help/wrr/r2027.0.0.0/en/wrr/PractitionersGuide/UnderstandingWeibullAnalysis.html — PTC Windchill Quality Solutions, 'Understanding Weibull Analysis': the shape-to-action table (burn-in and screening under 1; redesign only at 1; preventive replacement above 1) (fetched 2026-11-15)

import_sentence: In reliability engineering, a population of units written to the same design but of unknown individual quality is handled by fitting the hazard's shape in age — falling (defective units, screened by burn-in), flat (random failures, where burn-in and overhaul buy nothing and only redesign helps), rising (wear-out, scheduled replacement) — and letting the shape, not the level, choose the maintenance policy; carried into L4, that says a lesson written from one success- or failure-labelled trajectory is a shipped unit whose age is its retrieval count and whose failure is a memory-induced failure (the agent fails a task it solves with that lesson withheld), that the admission probes of FGSE are burn-in, the evidence-linked descent of WikiTrace is per-use inspection, and the certificate restarts, retirement rules and capacity bounds of 2610.17544, TrackRL and Library Drift are scheduled replacement, and that which of the three pays is decided by the shape of the per-use harm against the lesson's own use-age, with lesson frailty and store crowding separated, which none of them has measured.

predicts.statement: Setup: a self-evolving insight store (WikiTrace's released code, its insights-only arm: lessons distilled from success/failure-labelled trajectories, no evidence links; or a ReasoningBank-style store) on ALFWorld's 134 unseen tasks run for 3 passes in a fixed order, the actor (Qwen3.5-9B or Qwen3-30B-A3B) at its deployed sampling temperature, every retrieval logged. Units: lesson $\ell$, written after episode $e_\ell$; its $u$-th retrieval ($u = 1, 2, \ldots$) falls on task $t_{\ell u}$ with the store $M_{\ell u}$ at that moment. Paired harm: run the task $n = 4$ times with the retrieved set (one shared with-arm per task, as CoReMem shares its no-memory arm) and $n = 4$ times with lesson $\ell$ withheld, successes $a_{\ell u}$ and $c_{\ell u}$; $\hat\delta_{\ell u} = (c_{\ell u} - a_{\ell u}) / n$ is the lesson's induced harm on that use (positive: the agent does worse with the lesson). Ruler, non-parametric first: the mean harm $\bar\delta(U)$ by use-age bin $U \in \{1\}, \{2, 3\}, \{4\text{–}7\}, \{8+\}$ with a lesson-cluster bootstrap; parametric summary: $\mathbb{E}[\hat\delta_{\ell u} \mid z_\ell] = z_\ell\, \lambda\, u^{\beta - 1} |M_{\ell u}|^{\gamma}$ with $z_\ell$ a lesson frailty (mean 1, variance $\sigma^2$), $\lambda$ the level, $\beta$ the aging shape in the lesson's own use-age (the NHPP $b$ with use count as age), and $\gamma$ the crowding exponent on the store size, fitted on the positive-harm events with the frailty as a random effect. Control: a frozen-store arm (store frozen after pass 1; passes 2-3 replayed against it) in which $\beta = 1$ and $\gamma$ is undefined by construction because every use of a lesson is a draw from the same task distribution against the same store. P1 (shape): the bin means differ by at least 0.05 between $\{1\}$ and $\{8+\}$ in the growing-store arm and by under 0.03 in the frozen arm. P2 (frailty): $\sigma^2 \ge 1$, i.e. the top fifth of lessons by $z_\ell$ carry over half of the summed positive harm. P3 (burn-in leakage): with $p_\ell$ a lesson's per-use probability of a harm event at $\beta = 1$, $k$ admission probes catch it with probability $1 - (1 - p_\ell)^{k}$; the predicted share of harmful lessons that survive $k$ probes, $\mathbb{E}[(1 - p_\ell)^{k} \mid \text{harmful}]$, is reported for $k = 3, 10, 30$ and read against FGSE's 3.6% harmful committed updates. Also reported: the symmetric benefit $-\hat\delta$ by bin, so the ruler is two-sided, and the per-task with-arm's own replicate spread (the S12 noise CoReMem leaves unreported).
predicts.expected: Judgment, not evidence. Probability 0.4 that the hazard rises with use-age ($\beta$ in $[1.2, 1.8]$) and that the rise is absorbed by the store-size term ($\gamma > 0$ with $\beta$ falling into $[0.9, 1.1]$ once $|M|$ is in the model): a lesson is not degraded by its own age but by the company it is retrieved with (more co-retrieved lessons, more conflicts, more misapplication), which is Library Drift's 'false-positive injections' mechanism read at lesson grain. Probability 0.35 that the hazard is flat ($\beta \in [0.85, 1.15]$, $\gamma \approx 0$) with strong frailty: harm is a lesson property drawn per use at a constant rate, the population a mixture of a harmful minority and a harmless majority. Probability 0.25 that it falls ($\beta < 0.85$ after frailty): a lesson's early uses are the dangerous ones. Probability 0.6 for P2 in every case. Expected mechanism for the lean: ALFWorld tasks are drawn from a fixed distribution with no fact edits, so the only thing that changes between a lesson's first and tenth use is the store around it.
predicts.field_assumes: Four designs, four unmeasured shapes. FGSE 2611.14326 admits a lesson 'only after' target-transfer, falsification and archived-regression probes and reports a residual 3.6% of 'harmful committed updates': defects are at birth and a fixed probe battery finds them (falling hazard; burn-in works). WikiTrace 2611.14320 says degradation comes when the agent 'follows a lesson that is incorrect, or misapplies or misreads a valid one' and inspects at every use (per-use draw; flat hazard). 2610.17544 proves counters are poor change detectors under a model in which a memory's reliability is constant within an epoch and changes only 'when facts change' (flat within epochs, steps between; its ledger 'restarts the certificate when facts change'). TrackRL 2610.25126 protects young skills ('protecting skills whose limited evidence may conceal latent value during their incubation periods') and retires them 'once the model internalizes the corresponding capability' (rising, by internalization; and the opposite sign to burn-in for the young). Library Drift 2605.19576 names 'unbounded skill accumulation' causing 'retrieval degradation, false-positive injections' and fixes it with a bounded active cap (rising, by crowding), measured at library level as pass@1 over rounds, never per skill against its age. The reliability-engineering assumption is the reverse of all five: the shape is unknown until fitted, and the policy follows the shape.
predicts.belief_changing: If the rise is absorbed by store size (expected), lesson-grain harm is crowding: capacity or age bounds (Library Drift, REM's single-exposure eviction) are the right design, admission probing is sized by P3 and FGSE's residual is leakage, not a defect floor, and 2610.17544's constant-within-epoch null must carry a store-size term. If the hazard is flat with strong frailty, burn-in works only as a frailty screen and P3 says how many probes it takes (for $p = 0.1$, three probes catch 27%, thirty catch 96%), per-use inspection pays only on the frailty minority once identified, and expiry buys nothing. If the hazard falls after frailty is removed, the first few real uses are the whole admission test, TrackRL's protected incubation has the wrong sign, and WikiTrace's descent after age 3 is waste. If the hazard rises and is not absorbed by store size, a lesson is degraded by its own age at fixed store — a reading-drift mechanism no fetched source names — and self-evolving stores need age-based re-validation independent of fact edits. In every branch the 'memory-induced degradation' metric becomes a curve over use-age with a frailty share, not one rate.

identifiability: Random given: fixed task, fixed lesson text, fixed store state $M_{\ell u}$ at the moment of retrieval, fixed actor model and sampling, deterministic environment (ALFWorld and AppWorld return the same verdict for the same action sequence, so there is no environment luck term and the verifier is programmatic, not a judge). Whose temperature: the actor's at its deployed setting (RBC's protocol runs actors at 0.7; WikiTrace's setting is not in its abstract and is read from its code before the run); at actor temperature 0 each (task, store) pair has a fixed outcome up to serving noise, the paired harm is a 0/1 fact of the pair, $n = 1$ suffices, and the hazard is defined over the task stream, never over reruns. The writer's (reflector's) temperature does not enter the hazard, because the lesson text is held fixed once written; it enters the frailty distribution (which lessons get written) and is reported as a protocol term. Whose property: $z_\ell$ belongs to the lesson text under this actor; $\lambda$ to the (store, actor, task distribution) triple; $\beta$ and $\gamma$ to the protocol — use-age $u$ is a count under one retrieval policy (top-$k$ by similarity) and crowding is a property of the store growth rule, so a capacity-bounded store cannot show $\gamma$ by construction and the record reports $\beta$ per (memory system, retrieval policy, task order), with the task order randomized over 3 seeds so that age is not a proxy for a fixed task sequence. Degenerate-null guard: the frozen-store arm has $\beta = 1$ by construction; if the estimator returns a bin trend there, the estimator is confounded and the growing-store reading is void. Noise of the label: $\hat\delta_{\ell u}$ at $n = 4$ has standard error about $\sqrt{2 q (1 - q) / 4} \approx 0.35$ at $q = 0.5$, symmetric under the null, so the ruler is the signed mean harm by bin (about 375 events per bin, bin standard error about 0.02), never a binarized 'induced failure' event, whose false rate at $n = 3$ and $q = 0.5$ would be 0.25 (the S12 trap inside the ruler). Judge versus verifier: outcomes are the environment's verifier; no LLM judge anywhere in the probe.

probe.design: Step 1 (about 18 GPU-hours, 6 days including 3 of harness work): WikiTrace's released code (github.com/yukyeongleee/wikitrace), insights-only arm, on ALFWorld's 134 unseen tasks for 3 passes in a seeded order with a 9B or 30B-A3B actor under vLLM at the deployed temperature; log every (lesson, task) retrieval; at each task run the with-arm 4 times and, for each of the about 4 retrieved lessons, the withhold-one arm 4 times (about 20 episodes per task, about 8,000 episodes, about 1,500 (lesson, use) pairs); compute $\hat\delta_{\ell u}$, the bin means with lesson-cluster bootstrap, and the frailty / aging / crowding fit. Step 2 (about 10 GPU-hours, 2 days): the frozen-store arm (store frozen after pass 1, passes 2-3 replayed) as the null, and two more task orders for the growing store. Step 3 (1 day, no compute): P3 from the fitted $p_\ell$ distribution, read against FGSE's 3.6%. Optional step 4 (about $400 API or 25 GPU-hours): the same design on AppWorld with one API actor to check that the shape is not an ALFWorld fact.
probe.dollars: about $100 at H100 spot rates for steps 1-3; $400 more for the optional AppWorld arm
probe.days: 9 days: 3 of harness work, 3 of runs, 3 of analysis
probe.kills_if: Dead as a claim if the pooled mean harm over all uses is under 0.02 with the bootstrap interval's upper end under 0.04 (lesson-grain degradation too small to have a shape worth a design; the footnote is the per-retrieval harm rate on ALFWorld). Dead as a ruler if the frozen-store arm shows a bin trend whose interval excludes zero (age confounded with task order; the estimator is broken). Dead as an import if, with pooled harm above 0.02, every pair of bin means differs by under 0.03 and the frailty variance interval includes 0: flat and homogeneous, so burn-in, per-use inspection and expiry all buy nothing and the shape is not a lever — the result is a footnote that the four lifecycle designs are indistinguishable at benchmark scale.
