papers.title: Many Steps into One: Reasoning Contraction and the Limits of Safe Memory Reuse for LLM Agents
papers.trick: Treat a reused memory (template, skill, cached answer) as a bet whose verified outcomes feed a betting certificate against live reasoning, retire it with a likelihood-ratio CUSUM when its facts change, and prove that the success/failure counters of ExpeL and ACE are badly tuned change detectors (7-73x more stale answers).
papers.did_not_do: Its model holds a memory's reliability constant within an epoch and moves it only at an edit ('until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong'; 'restarts the certificate when facts change'), so the aging shape is $\beta = 1$ by assumption, the changes are injected edits on multi-hop QA and code with an exact verifier, and the per-use harm is never read against the memory's own use-age or the store's size; its one survival estimate (Kaplan-Meier) is of the delay from an edit to retirement, not of a memory's time-to-first-harm; no frailty term, no burn-in computation (full text grepped: 'hazard', 'bathtub', 'burn-in', 'infant', 'wear', 'Weibull' absent).

papers.title: Trackable Skill Library Lifecycle Management for Agentic Reinforcement Learning (TrackRL)
papers.trick: Inside each GRPO group inject each skill at random so that within-group contrasts on the same task give the skill's causal contribution, accumulate it with reliability weights, and run every skill through an evidence-gated state machine (admission, protected incubation, retention, retirement, removal) under a soft capacity bound.
papers.did_not_do: Holds the per-skill counterfactual estimator this import needs and never reads it against the skill's use-age: its 'aging' is the policy's internalization during RL ('that gap may narrow or shift as the policy evolves'), its lifecycle is a state machine with hand-set evidence thresholds, and 'protected incubation' presupposes that young skills are under-evidenced rather than over-hazardous, the opposite bet to burn-in, without a measurement of the early hazard that would decide between them (full text grepped: no 'hazard', 'lifetime', 'survival', 'use count'). Third: FGSE 2611.14326 (burn-in at admission; residual 3.6% reported as a rate, not as a function of probe count and per-use harm). Fourth: Library Drift 2605.19576 (crowding named — 'unbounded skill accumulation ... retrieval degradation, false-positive injections' — and fixed by a bounded active cap; measured as library pass@1 over 100 rounds, never per skill against age; 'premature retirement' shown to harm). Fifth: 2610.32578 ('harness lessons can outlive the failures they were written to fix ... tools that evolve a harness add lessons faster than they retire them'; a one-repository six-week ledger, no hazard). Sixth: Repo2Skill-Evo 2608.21964 (wear-out by releases, measured as a skill-maintenance F1). Seventh: 2604.12007 (two-counter Memory Worth converging to an associational success probability 'under a stationary retrieval regime'). Pre-window precedents with their tricks: survival and Weibull for agent horizons (Ord 2505.05115; the W42 S7xF9 record); gauge R&R for agent scores (2610.00651, 2608.11323); the anytime-valid admission gate (PACE 2606.08106; the W42 S12xF3 record, closed as already-made).

nearest.verdict: Not made. The lifecycle vocabulary is dense (incubation, retention, retirement, removal, staleness, drift, forgetting: about 20 of 181 Q2 hits), the per-lesson counterfactual contrast exists (TrackRL's random withholding; CoReMem's with/without), staleness-as-change-point exists (2610.17544), crowding is named at library level (2605.19576) and admission probing exists (FGSE, SkillForge, PACE); no fetched source fits the per-use harm of a lesson against the lesson's own use-age, separates lesson frailty from aging from store crowding, runs the frozen-store null, or computes the burn-in leakage of an admission battery from the per-use harm rate. It is not a rename of the W42 S12xF3 import (that was the admission gate's error control, made by PACE); it is not a rename of Library Drift (that is a library-level symptom and a recipe; this is a per-unit hazard shape that can come out against crowding); and it is not another memory recipe (no gate, no store, no retrieval policy is proposed; the output is a shape and the policy it selects).

reason_for_pick: S12 is this week's live L4 shape through card 2611.17316 (a memory's value as a 3-vs-4 with/without contrast with its noise unreported, sign flipping under another harness) and the two kept seeds 2611.14320 (memory-induced degradation from lessons inferred off success/failure labels) and 2611.14326 (lessons admitted only after falsification and regression probes; 3.6% harmful commits). F9 is in Jacob's evaluable set; its gauge-R&R half is spent (W42 S7xF9 for scores; W45 S3xF9 for the compressor, killed because the design was in print), so the pick was the field's other half — the bathtub, the power-law hazard and the burn-in / inspection / replacement policy table — which the W42 and W45 records never carried, applied to the lesson lifecycle where four designs in print presuppose four different shapes. The W42 S12xF3 pair was already closed (PACE), so the admission gate's error control is excluded from this import by construction.

scorecard.target_value: In print: WikiTrace 2611.14320 ('memory-induced degradation, where an agent fails on tasks it would solve without memory, often because it follows a lesson that is incorrect, or misapplies or misreads a valid one'); FGSE 2611.14326 ('when an experience-derived behavioral update should be admitted into persistent agent state'; 'harmful committed updates to 3.6%'); 2610.32578 ('tools that evolve a harness add lessons faster than they retire them, so they should re-test their rules from time to time and retire the obsolete ones'); TrackRL 2610.25126 ('protecting skills whose limited evidence may conceal latent value during their incubation periods'); Library Drift 2605.19576 ('unbounded skill accumulation without outcome-driven lifecycle management causes retrieval degradation, false-positive injections'); 2610.17544 ('A contracted memory saves reasoning steps and errors until its facts change, then quietly answers wrong'). Who pays: builders of self-evolving memory choosing between admission probes, per-use inspection and expiry; teams running rule files and auto-memory in coding agents; evaluators who report one degradation number.

scorecard.density_and_ownership: L4 is the densest lane (about one memory or compaction paper a week); lifecycle papers ran at about two a month in October 2026 (TrackRL 2610.25126, SkillForge 2610.09832, Selm 2610.24630, 2610.32322, 2610.32578, 2610.27377, 2610.17544). Occupied: lifecycle state machines with incubation and retirement (TrackRL, SkillForge, 2605.10923), retirement from failures and its judge dependence (2607.07436, 2605.22148), staleness as a change-point with certificates (2610.17544), skills going stale across releases (2608.21964), crowding at library level (2605.19576), admission probing (FGSE 2611.14326; PACE 2606.08106, W42), the per-lesson with/without contrast (TrackRL; CoReMem 2611.17316), associational counters (2604.12007). Unoccupied in every fetched source: the per-use harm of a lesson read against its own use-age, the frailty / aging / crowding split, the frozen-store null, and the burn-in leakage of an admission battery. Natural first movers: the TrackRL authors (their logs hold per-skill contrasts over training steps), the 2610.17544 authors (ledger with use counts), the WikiTrace authors (the harness); the re-open test is asking them. Race window: about two lifecycle papers a month against a 9-day probe on a public harness; proper-shaped from the solo position, golden only if the shape replicates across harnesses.
scorecard.why_now: WikiTrace (2026-11-10) named memory-induced degradation at lesson grain and released code with an insights-only arm, so the per-lesson withholding is a configuration change; FGSE (2026-11-10) published an admission-battery residual (3.6%) that a hazard-and-probe-count formula can predict; TrackRL (2026-10-18) made within-group random withholding the standard per-skill estimator; 2610.17544 (2026-10-13) wrote the constant-within-epoch assumption down and brought Kaplan-Meier into the lane, so the survival vocabulary is already there; CoReMem (2026-11-12) defined a memory's value as the with/without next-task contrast and left its noise unreported.
scorecard.register_and_what_it_is_not: Measurement register: a hazard shape (three bins and a power law) with a frailty share and a crowding exponent, a mechanism (harm is a lesson property, a per-use draw, or the company a lesson keeps) and a policy consequence (probe, inspect or expire; the probe count from $1 - (1 - p)^{k}$). It is not a new memory system, not an admission gate (the W42 S12xF3 import, made by PACE), not a staleness detector (2610.17544), not a library-level drift diagnosis (2605.19576), and not a run-to-run variance study of agent scores: the unit is one lesson at one use, and the question is how its harm moves with its age.
